newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tobishima shares up on likely restructuring pact.
newsitem.headline: Tobishima shares up on likely restructuring pact.

text.p: Shares in Tobishima Corp rose in Monday morning trade after the firm said it had set a clear course for a basic agreement with its private banks on its restructuring plan.
As of 0021 GMT, the shares were up two yen at 235 yen with turnover of 301,000.

Tobishima announced on Friday that it had set a clear course for reaching a basic agreement with all private financial institutions concerned, but that negotiations with public financial firms would continue.

Under the restructuring plan drawn up last year, debt-ridden Tobishima asked its creditors to reduce their claims against the construction firm for its group companies' debt to 100 billion yen from about 740 billion yen.

Tobishima president Shoichiro Ishihara, meanwhile, told a news conference on Friday that a final agreement is likely to be reached in early April on the restructuring plan, which he said should include a cut in creditor banks' claims against Tobishima for its group firms' debts as originally planned.
